title: Framework addresses BIOS update issues bricking Ryzen 7040 laptops
summary: Framework has acknowledged reports that a BIOS update (version 3.20) for its Ryzen 7040-series Framework Laptop 13 is causing some systems to become non-bootable. The update, released in June 2026, was intended to add support for new hardware features and fix existing issues but has resulted in bricked devices for a subset of users. Framework is investigating the root cause and offering out-of-warranty motherboard replacements for affected customers. Additionally, the company is introducing a 'Crisis Recovery Mode' to help recover failed updates in future BIOS releases.
key_points: Framework released BIOS 3.20 for Ryzen 7040-series Framework Laptop 13 in June 2026, aiming to add features and fix bugs.
Multiple users reported the update stalling during installation, resulting in bricked laptops that cannot be powered down or rebooted.
Framework confirmed a 'small percentage' of devices are affected and is investigating the root cause.
Some users were initially told they needed a paid motherboard replacement if out of warranty, but Framework is now making exceptions for confirmed BIOS-related failures.
Framework is introducing 'Crisis Recovery Mode' in future BIOS updates to enable recovery from failed updates.
A blogger suggested the issue may stem from a software bug causing erratic memory behavior during the update process.
Reports of BIOS update issues with Ryzen 7040-based Framework Laptop 13 devices date back to at least March 2025.
